newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope calls on world to end Zaire "catastrophe".
newsitem.headline: Pope calls on world to end Zaire "catastrophe".

text.p: Pope John Paul said on Wednesday he was following events in north-east Zaire with "unspeakable sorrow" and called on world to step up its help.
"I sincerely hope the international community will do all in its power to bring help effectively to the catastrophe which is raging," the Pontiff said in an address to pilgrims in St Peter's Square.

"With unspeakable sorrow, I am following events in north-eastern Zaire, where ferocious fighting and looting has forced thousands of Rwandan and Burundian refugees, especially the elderly, women and children, into an aimless flight," the Pope said.
"It is an interminable tragedy... It is agonising to see how human beings, who are sons of God and brothers of ours, are being treated."

More than a week of fighting has driven some half a million Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees out of camps in east Zaire. Aid workers said Rwandan and Zairean troops traded mortar and machinegun fire across their border on Wednesday.
"I pray for guns to be silenced, for hatred and ethnic rivalries to be placated and that an end to be put to the shameful manhunt that is taking the place of negotiations," the Pope said.
